description:
`if b == ?;` works today (?; is an integer literal), but comparing a byte range against "Hamburg" or emitting a separator needs a literal [u8]. Proposed: a binary literal `"abc"` in a kernel body (and `<<1, 2, 3>>` with integer segments) lowers to a static const uint8_t[] view {data, len}, type [u8], not owned (read-only, cannot be returned). Elixir meaning: the literal itself. Module attributes holding a binary (defk-ivt) should lower the same way, so do this together with or right after defk-ivt. Non-byte segments (floats, utf32) are rejected with a rewrite.

Done when: a kernel can index and `len` a literal, pass it to a helper, and compare its bytes in a loop; Elixir mode agrees; a literal in a yielding loop survives resume (static data needs no rebinding, add a test anyway).
title: String literals as [u8] constants in kernel bodies
